models_evaluated: deep learning arterial waveform-based intraoperative hypotension prediction model

links.outcome: Alarms per hour and positive predictive value on biased versus unbiased test datasets
links.effect: For 5-min-ahead prediction with the DL model, unbiased vs biased testing gave 18.1 vs 10.8 alarms per hour (P<0.001) and PPV 0.068 vs 0.937 (P<0.001).
links.quote: For the prediction of intraoperative hypotension 5 min before the event with the DL model, using the unbiased vs the biased testing dataset resulted in 18.1 vs 10.8 alarms per hour (P<0.001) and a positive predictive value of 0.068 vs 0.937 (P<0.001).

links.outcome: Performance of DL model versus simpler MAP-only model on same data
links.effect: The DL model statistically outperformed the MAP-only model, but the difference was not clinically meaningful.
links.quote: Although the DL model statistically performed better than the MAP-only model, the difference between the two models was not clinically meaningful.

screen.reason: The study empirically tests how a key validation/evaluation practice (testing on a clinically realistic, unselected dataset vs. an artificially filtered/biased dataset) drastically changes observed model performance (PPV drops from 0.937 to 0.068).
